subject: doomscrollers
one_liner: A long-form publishing platform that meters your intake of bad news down to a level two clinicians have described as survivable.
brand_voice_notes: Regulated-substance deadpan. The company genuinely believes it is a pharmaceutical manufacturer and that reading is a route of administration. Copy is written the way a carton is written: flat declaratives, dosage language, warnings that are technically reassurances. Never scolds the reader for doomscrolling and never celebrates it either. Treats 340 articles a day as a clinical baseline to taper from, not a problem to solve. Numbers are specific, unrounded, and quietly alarming. No exclamation marks anywhere. The founder tone is a compliance officer who thinks this is going well.

hero.sub: Bleakly is a reading platform for people who were going to read all of it anyway. We do not stop you. We seal each article in its own cell, meter the intake, and print the amount on the outside of the box.

features.title: The titration ladder
features.blurb: Nobody quits at once. You enter at your measured baseline of 340 articles a day and step down to 310 over eleven months, unsupervised, at a rate our advisory board called defensible.

features.title: Blister-pack feed
features.blurb: Every article is sealed in its own foil cell. Pressing one out is deliberate, loud, and permanent. Tuesday cannot be re-read. Several users have asked. Tuesday cannot be re-read.

features.title: Contraindications engine
features.blurb: Cross-references today's headlines against everything else you are currently taking. Flags the four that interact badly with your group chat and the one that should not be combined with a family dinner.

demo_screen_concept: The Dosing Console: a foil blister-pack grid of today's twelve sealed article cells. Each cell is pressable and pops with a foil-tear animation to reveal a headline, a severity grade (I through IV), and a side-effects list with frequencies. A daily dose meter fills toward the prescribed ceiling as cells are opened. A titration slider from 'mild unease' to 'structural collapse' refilters the grid to only the cells at or below that grade. Pressing two cells from the same interaction group raises a contraindication banner. Once the ceiling is reached the sheet seals and a lockout countdown replaces the grid.

design_direction.style: Regulated pharmaceutical packaging and patient-information leaflet, blister-pack daylight mode. The page is staged as the printed carton and folded insert of a company that manufactures reading as a controlled substance. Surfaces are plastic and foil rather than paper: no deckled edges, no paper grain, no drawing-sheet chrome, no bento lattice, no glass, no blur, no gradients that read as light. The ground is a cold pale eucalyptus (#E5EBE3) with every content surface a flat optic-white card at 3px radius, hairline-bordered in a 1px pharmacy green, never shadowed. Depth comes only from the foil motif: a horizontal brushed-silver band built from a repeating-linear-gradient of five greys, used as the top edge of every card the way foil backs a blister sheet. The core motif is the cell: a rounded-rectangle capsule dome with a 999px radius on the short axis, rendered in optic white against green, used as the list bullet, the feature index, the pricing tier badge and the testimonial avatar frame, so every discrete item on the page reads as one unit of dose. The second motif is the regulatory band: a full-bleed strip of hazard amber (#E2A008) with 900-weight uppercase green type knocked into it, quarantined strictly to warnings, ceilings and the lockout state, never used for navigation or delight. Deep pharmacy green (#10553A) is the sole flood colour: the wordmark, every primary CTA, the section rules, the leaflet body rules and the cell fills. Type is set the way a carton is set: display in Archivo at 700-800 with -0.02em tracking and uppercase micro-labels at 0.18em, body in Source Sans 3 at a leaflet-tight 1.55, and every quantity, lot number, grade and timer in Spline Sans Mono with tabular figures. Section headings are preceded by a numbered clause marker (01, 02, 03) in mono, as on a folded insert. Nothing is rounded above 3px except the cell domes and the pills. Nothing glows.
design_direction.archetype: Long-form publishing platform product page staged as pharmaceutical packaging: carton face as hero, folded patient-information leaflet as the features and warnings body, dosage table as pricing, and a printed batch record as the footer.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Mechanical and short. Cells depress 2px on press with no bounce. The foil band on a card wipes left-to-right over 220ms on reveal. The amber regulatory band slides down from behind its card edge over 180ms and never fades. Dose meters fill with a linear transform over 400ms, never eased, because a meter that eases looks like it is being generous. Hover states change fill and border only, never scale. All motion is suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: The hero is a carton face, not a banner: a single optic-white panel centred at 1080px max width, silver foil band across its top edge, a mono lot line reading the product code and net contents above the headline, the headline set entirely in Archivo 800 at clamp(2.6rem, 7vw, 5.4rem) in pharmacy green with no accented word, since amber stays quarantined to the warning band, the subhead capped at 62 characters per line directly beneath, and the primary CTA as a solid green pill flanked by a mono line stating the measured baseline. A four-across strip of mono spec pairs (route of administration, baseline, ceiling, review interval) runs along the bottom edge of the panel as printed carton small type. The full-bleed amber regulatory band sits immediately below the carton, running the standing warning.

images.rationale: Hero skipped: the direction is a printed carton face, and a photograph inside it would break the packaging conceit. Demo assets skipped: the Dosing Console is a foil blister grid built entirely in CSS, so there is nothing photo-shaped in it. Full budget spent on three testimonial headshots of doomscrollers, shot as flat clinical patient-leaflet portraiture, which is the one slot on the page where a real face earns its space.
